player_base.design_purpose: Baseline survivability before any equipment. armour_reduction_scale controls how fast armour approaches full physical reduction (reduction = armour / (armour + scale)); resistance_cap_percent stops resistance stacking from trivialising elemental threats.

shelter.design_purpose: Resting in a shelter is the health-regeneration route (owner playtest 2 Sep 2026: 'you need some passive health regeneration or a way to get health regened'). A shelter is an enclosed room - the sim flood-fills the space around the player through open cells, stopped by placed walls, floors, blocks and by terrain, and it is a shelter when the fill closes before max_room_cells build cells without reaching open sky. Regen starts settle_rounds after the last hit taken and pays regen_life_per_round (per round_seconds of combat_realtime.json), so a hut is worth building on day one, a dug-out hollow with a slab over its mouth counts, and a mob that breaks in stops the rest. Out in the open, nothing regenerates: the deprivation the owner asked for at the start stays.

encroachment.design_purpose: Base threat as pressure, never demolition (owner steer 3 Sep 2026: a timber house is a house at every tier, and the threat should not vanish at higher tiers either). Once the player has a home - a shelter they have rested in - a pack settles into a nest on the fringe ring (fringe_min_m..fringe_max_m from home) every settle_seconds, up to max_nests, never within spacing_m of another nest or a fresh scar. A standing nest grows a tier every growth_seconds (tiers lists its pack; the top tier brings a shrieker to call packs to your walls), and a fallen member returns after respawn_seconds while the nest stands. Within blight_radius_m rest in the shelter pays uneasy_rest_multiplier of its regen. The exploit guard (owner, 3 Sep): only nest_loot_fraction of nest-born kills drop anything and tearing a nest down drops nothing, so a nest is a nuisance to end, not a crop to grow - waiting only makes the neighbourhood worse. A cleared spot scars for scar_seconds. Nests are not saved: a loaded game starts quiet.

enemies.design_purpose: Basic fodder that teaches area clearing
Introduces fire damage in small doses before the boss
Cheap but quick; the hastened weakness makes packs of these frightening
Slow hill guardian that makes stone and iron country feel owned; killing it IS mining, so combat feeds construction directly

The aggro-chainer (D-012, named in the roadmap): it hangs back and SCREAMS - every idle mob in scream radius joins the chase, so a pack with a shrieker recruits the biome. Kill it first or fight everything it can see. Barely dangerous alone; its page chance is the bounty on its head.
The cave dweller: quick in the tunnels where there is no room to kite, guarding the underground iron. Meeting one in the dark is the cost of the richer veins.
The fen's wall: slow, thick, and it does not bleed (nothing to open in that hide). You do not train a lurker, you walk around it - and a wisp behind it makes the walk cost.
The fen's sting: a fast skirmisher that keeps its distance and pecks. Alone it is a nuisance; behind a lurker it is the reason to bring a projectile.
The wastes' skirmisher: burning, quick, ignite-proof. It is what makes fire resistance matter outside the trial.
The wastes' armoured line: slow, heavy, and fire does nothing to a hollow suit. Cold and bleed are the answers; it is the first mob that asks the build a question the whelps did not.
Life beyond hostiles (owner, 3 Sep 2026): grazers that bolt when you come near and never bite. Hunting them is a choice, and the hide is the start of a leather line.

elite_modifiers.design_purpose: The anti-Glacier elite: chill never sticks, so the freeze-shatter sentence needs a second answer in the pack (D-016 statuses meet resistance, PoE-style).
The anti-Wildfire elite: it will not burn, and its death is a fire nova - stand back for the kill or eat the burst. Positioning is the counter, as always (D-012).
The anvil: bleeds find no vein and the life pool is a wall. Slow enough to disengage from - fighting it is a choice you commit to.
Pure pressure: faster than you in a straight line. Chill and pits are the counters - the grammar answers what stats cannot.

design_purpose_elites: Wave 3 elite prefixes: worldgen's danger rings decide who spawns elite (farther out, more often); each interacts with the D-016 status grammar rather than only multiplying numbers, and each pays triple gear/page chance plus an extra loot pass - elites are why you hunt the far rings. Trial rooms do not roll elites yet (the dungeon pass owns that).

gathering_sites.design_purpose: Safe early gathering; controls how long shelter and fuel work takes
Iron source with real risk, so open-world death rules matter; reinforcing the mine (order world effect) removes the ambushes

open_world_death.design_purpose: Open-world death drops carried inventory at the site for recovery (D-006); permanent equipment is never dropped

design_purpose_loot: Every mob pays out into the survival economy (fuel, ore, stone, coin) so fighting is never dead time next to gathering. Three kinds of entry: {item,min,max,chance} materials; {gear: rarity, tier, chance} a rolled piece on any base (D-014); {skill_page: true, chance} a page teaching one skill the player does not know yet, weighted by skills.json drop_weight (D-016). Page chances are set so a first hour of hunting finds one or two skills; the mob pass will move them onto elites.
design_purpose_pacing: Long fights (owner, 3 Sep 2026: 'we get too powerful too quick ... more like early MMOs, lots of mobs and it takes a while to kill things', combat should 'start a bit more powerful' - the swing stays, the life bars grow). Mob life is two and a half times the first cut and mob damage seven tenths, player numbers untouched: a day-one whelp takes three heavy blows instead of two-and-a-bit, a pack is a thirty-second fight where spacing and the sweep matter, and the first Keen mace no longer ends era one. The trial's bosses keep their numbers; the oracle (tools/balance) holds their win rates in band.
